findings.title: Bulk sensitive data exposure
findings.description: An endpoint returns a list of records with personal or financial fields, and it is either reachable without a token or not documented, so nobody reviewed what it hands out.
findings.detail: GET /home (frontend) returns a list with financial fields
findings.owasp: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
findings.recommendation: Reduce fields and require an admin role on /home.
mitigation: Return only the fields the client needs (response schema / DTO, not the raw record).
Paginate with a hard maximum and require an admin role for bulk export.
Log every bulk export with the caller identity.

findings.title: Shadow endpoint (running, not documented)
findings.description: The endpoint receives traffic but is in no API specification, so it was never part of a design review.
findings.detail: GET /home (frontend) is served but in no spec
findings.recommendation: Document or remove GET /home in frontend.
mitigation: Either document the endpoint (and review it) or remove it.
Fail CI when a service serves routes missing from its spec (compare traffic with spec).

findings.title: Login has no visible brute-force protection
findings.description: The login endpoint returned failures but never a 429 or lockout, and no rate-limiting directive in the gateway or Ingress configuration covers it, so password guessing is not being slowed down.
findings.detail: POST /login (frontend): 15 failed logins, no 429 seen
evidence: no rate-limiting directive on its gateway route or Ingress
findings.recommendation: Add rate limiting and lockout to /login.
mitigation: Rate-limit login per account and per IP (e.g. 5 failures / 15 min) and return 429.
Add MFA for privileged accounts and alert on failure spikes.

findings.title: Secret stored in plaintext in the deployment manifest
findings.description: An environment variable with a secret-looking name has its value written directly in the manifest, so anyone with read access to the repo or cluster config has it.
findings.detail: TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS is written in plaintext in the userservice manifest
evidence: env TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS: source=plaintext (value not copied by the extractor)
findings.recommendation: Move TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS of userservice into a Secret and rotate it.
mitigation: Move the value into a Kubernetes Secret (or a vault) and reference it with secretKeyRef.
Rotate the exposed value: it is already in version control history.
Add a CI check that fails on plaintext env values with secret-like names.
findings.snippet:
env:
  - name: JWT_SECRET
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: {name: shoplite-secrets, key: jwt-secret}

findings.title: Public entry serves the API without TLS
findings.description: The public entry (Ingress, load balancer, Istio Gateway or published port) has no TLS, so Authorization headers and personal data sent through it can be read or replayed on the network. The evidence says how many public endpoints carried them in this capture.
findings.detail: LoadBalancer Service frontend serves the API over plain HTTP
findings.recommendation: Enable TLS on LoadBalancer Service frontend.
mitigation: Terminate TLS at the ingress (tls: section + certificate) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Send Strict-Transport-Security so browsers never fall back to HTTP.

findings.title: Credential passed in the URL query string

factors: likelihood -1: reachable only inside the cluster

findings.title: No network segmentation for the service
findings.description: No NetworkPolicy selects this workload, so every pod in the cluster can call it. One compromised pod can move laterally.
findings.detail: accounts-db accepts traffic from any pod
evidence: callers seen in traces: none (only external clients)
findings.recommendation: Add a NetworkPolicy for accounts-db allowing only: the ingress controller.
mitigation: Add a default-deny NetworkPolicy for the namespace, then allow only the callers seen in traces.

findings.title: Service-to-service call accepted without credentials
findings.description: Another microservice calls this endpoint without any credential and it succeeds, so any pod that can reach it can do the same (no zero-trust between services).
findings.detail: frontend -> GET /login (userservice) with no credential
factors: likelihood -1: reachable only inside the cluster
evidence: no mTLS enforced for userservice (no STRICT PeerAuthentication or mesh injection)
findings.recommendation: Require service identity (mTLS or a service token) on /login in userservice.
mitigation: Authenticate workloads to each other: mTLS through a service mesh, or signed service tokens.
Authorize per caller: only order-service may call /charge, for example.
findings.snippet:
# Istio: require mTLS and allow only order-service
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
spec:
  rules:
  - from:
    - source: {principals: ["cluster.local/ns/shoplite/sa/order-service"]}

findings.title: Container can run as root
findings.description: Nothing stops the container process from running as UID 0 (runAsUser: 0, or no runAsNonRoot).
findings.detail: accounts-db does not set runAsNonRoot
factors: likelihood -1: service reachable only inside the cluster
findings.recommendation: Run accounts-db as a non-root user.
mitigation: Set runAsNonRoot: true and a non-zero runAsUser.
Build images with a non-root USER.
